$comment: Relay multi-key rejection classifier (upstream shapes read from gateway source at fixed commits). One pure function per end: iOS RelayKeyAccess.classify(status:body:), Android RelayKeyAccess.classify(status, body), Web classifyRelayKeyAccess(status, body). It runs on a non-2xx relay response that arrived before any output, BEFORE the capability rejection loop (negative-cache.v1.json). Outcomes: `model_access_denied` = this key may not use this model (another key might) -> record the denial on the model for the bound key, do NOT write a capability negative cache entry, do NOT fall back to another protocol; `key_invalid` = the key itself is rejected (401, or an expired-key code); `key_limited` = balance / quota / rate limit (402, 429, or a 403 whose body carries a quota or balance code); `none` = not about the key, the existing paths decide. Body signals are matched case-insensitively as substrings of the raw body; a bare `model` / `group` / `not found` word is NOT a signal (capability rejections such as 'model does not support image input' and route-level 404s must stay `none`). done-hub folds token-model denial into 503 and cannot be told apart from a busy upstream, so 5xx is always `none`. Test names: KEY-ACCESS-<caseId>.

phrases: is not available for this group
is not supported for current token
do not have access to the model
does not have access to model

signals.precedence: statuses 401 / 402 / 429 decide first; then a 403 carrying a keyInvalid or keyLimited code; then modelAccessDenied (status in its list AND a code or phrase present); everything else none

sendCases.$comment: Production-path proof: a relay chat send of an enabled model bound to key `k-claude` (with an image attached) gets this pre-output rejection. Expect: the model records the denial for `k-claude`; no negative-cache entry is written for any level; no second request on another protocol; the message fails with the upstream error (no silent key switch).
Production-path proof: 401 on a send marks the bound key's status invalid (with http status and time); the model is not marked denied.

Production-path proof: a delivered send on a single-key connection (no relayKeys stored) records the primary's status: relayKeys becomes the one-entry list [{id: initial, apiKey: "", status ok}]; no model key fields are written.
Production-path proof: 401 on a send of a single-key connection marks the primary invalid in a one-entry relayKeys list.

generationCases.$comment: Key status from a generation request : one pure function per end, iOS RelayKeyAccess.generationStatus(status:body:), Android RelayKeyAccess.generationStatus(status, body), Web relayGenerationKeyStatus(status, body); status null = network / no response. 2xx -> ok; classify key_invalid -> invalid; key_limited -> limited; everything else (model_access_denied, route-level rejection, client gate, capability rejection, 5xx, network) -> null = leave the key status alone, because it says nothing about the key. Writers: chat send (incl. tool loops), 1-token reverify (incl. after an edit save), lazy probe / re-probe, every capability-test request, catalog refresh (catalogCases mapping, single key too). Not writers: draft 'Test connection' and add-flow step-1 verification (the catalog refresh after saving writes). The status goes on the key the request actually used (the model's effective key; a connection-level verification uses its sample model's effective key), only when state / httpStatus changes, and is dropped when the connection identity changed meanwhile. Test names: KEY-ACCESS-GEN-<caseId>; production paths RL2-KEYSTATUS-NN (same name on all three ends).
